title: Quantifying the reproductive progression of sunflower using FIJI (Image J)
author: Ochogavía

steps.title: Download FIJI (ImageJ)
steps.instruction: Visit https://imagej.nih.gov/ij/download.html and download the Windows version bundled with 32‑bit Java (version ij153).

steps.title: Install FIJI on Windows
steps.instruction: Save the installer to a folder named FIJI.app on the desktop, run it, follow the setup wizard, and click Finish. The download and installation take approximately 30 minutes.

steps.title: Launch FIJI
steps.instruction: Run the FIJI application; the menu bar and toolbar should appear on the desktop.

steps.title: Open capitulum image
steps.instruction: From the File menu choose Open and select the JPEG photograph of a sunflower capitulum taken at the appropriate developmental stage (R5.1‑R5.8 for disc‑flower counting, R6 for seed estimation). The image opens in a separate window.

steps.title: Measure external diameter
steps.instruction: Select the Straight‑line tool, draw a line across the outer edge of the capitulum, then choose Analyze → Measure (or press Ctrl+M). Record the pixel length of the external circumference and note the phenophase of the disc flowers present in this outer crown.

steps.title: Measure inner crown diameters
steps.instruction: Repeat the previous step for each inner circular crown (middle Ø2 and inner Ø3) that corresponds to the different disc‑flower phenophases; record each diameter in pixels and the associated phenophase.

steps.title: Convert image to 8‑bit
steps.instruction: Choose Image → Type → 8‑bit to change the colour image to an 8‑bit grayscale image.

steps.title: Adjust image threshold
steps.instruction: Open Image → Adjust → Threshold (or press Ctrl+Shift+T) and manually move the sliders until all inflorescences are visible as white spots on a black background. Remember that phenophases E3 and E4 appear as two white spots per flower.

steps.title: Binarize with Watershed
steps.instruction: Select Process → Binary → Watershed to separate touching particles after thresholding.

steps.title: Determine particle size range
steps.instruction: Zoom into the processed image, use the Oval selection tool to outline a single disc‑flower spot, then Analyze → Measure (Ctrl+M) to obtain its area. Repeat for the largest disc‑flower spot. Record the smallest and largest particle areas; these values define the size range for later particle analysis.

steps.title: Analyze particles in outer crown
steps.instruction: Using the Oval tool, draw a circle that matches the external diameter (Ø1). Choose Analyze → Analyze Particles, set the size range to the values obtained in the previous step, set Show = Nothing, tick Display Results, and run. Record the particle number (PN Ø1).

steps.title: Analyze particles in inner crowns
steps.instruction: Repeat the previous step for the middle circle (Ø2) and the inner circle (Ø3) using their respective diameters. Record PN Ø2 and PN Ø3.

steps.title: Calculate disc‑flower numbers
steps.instruction: Compute the number of disc flowers for each phenophase as follows: • E1 = PN Ø3 (smallest circle). • E2 = PN Ø2 – PN Ø3. • E3 = (PN Ø1 – PN Ø2) ÷ 2 (divide by two because each E3 flower appears as two spots). • Total disc flowers = E1 + E2 + E3. Perform the subtraction three independent times to obtain three technical replicates.

steps.title: Protocol 2 – Prepare seed‑count image
steps.instruction: Open a JPEG image taken at the R6 stage (all disc flowers are at phenophase E4). Then repeat steps 7–9 (8‑bit conversion, threshold adjustment, Watershed) and step 10 (determine particle size range).

steps.title: Count seed‑representing particles
steps.instruction: Draw a circle matching the external diameter (Ø1) of the capitulum, run Analyze → Analyze Particles with the size range from step 10, Show = Nothing, Display Results. Record the particle number (PN Ø1).

steps.title: Convert particle count to seed number
steps.instruction: Divide PN Ø1 by 2 because each developing seed appears as two stigmatic spots in the E4 phenotype. Repeat the counting three times to obtain three technical replicates.

steps.title: Optional: curved receptacle correction
steps.instruction: If the receptacle is curved, carefully remove the corolla, stamens, and style/stigma from the image so that only the ovary is visible before thresholding; the particle count will then directly estimate seed number.

description: Sunflower is today the third leading oilseed crop in the world, along with soybean and rapeseed [3]. It is the second-most important crop based on hybrid breeding and the fifth-largest oilseed crop in the world [9]. Genetic improvement is a critical factor for this crop productivity optimization and breeding programs require an exhaustive knowledge of reproductive biology. Some sunflower open-pollinated cultivars and wild populations are self-incompatible and are mostly cross-pollinated by insects [2]. With a background of self-incompatibility and seed production dependent on insect vectors, breeding programs have contributed to improving yield over open-pollinated cultivars by producing high levels of self-compatibility in hybrids. Some floral visitors, like pollinators (bees, bumbles, flies, some wasps, etc.), benefit the plant reproduction, but the predators (spiders, some wasps, some beetles, etc.) can damage and interferes the seed production [10]. The insect attraction/repellence is affected by the number of disc flowers achieving the anthesis phenophase E3, where pollen is available for visitors [4], [5],7]. Therefore, the quantification of the number of disc flowers at each phenophase that are constituting the capitula at each reproductive stage will be useful for correlation analysis in agroecological studies that evaluate the interaction of floral visitors and the reproductive development of this crop. Moreover, the estimation of the number of seeds in the capitula of plants at the field would anticipate the seed yield and reduce the time and resources consumed in breeding programs for cultivated sunflower. However, a previous characterization of the seed set and the number of flowers per capitulum should be done for each genotype before applying Protocol 2. Protocol 1 and 2 allow estimating the number of sunflower disc flowers or seeds at a particular developmental stage in the field cultivated plants.
